title: Claire's Cassard and Peterson family of musicians
summary: Claire explains her Cassard relatives (Jules Cassard, Joe, Leo, Raymond Burke's mother, the Petersons) and who played which instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But you're kind of the Petersons too.
My mother was a Cassard. Her mother was a Cassard.
Yes.
And Jules Cassard was her brother and he wrote Angry. And he's getting royalties. Yeah, he's living in Florida and he's getting royalties on Angry.
Still following the horses?
I believe he does that in the winter. Oh. He's retired now.
Oh, yeah.

And I'm also related to Raymond Burke and Harold Peterson and George Peterson. My grandfather was Jules Cassard, played the violin in the French Opera. And he taught Uncle George Peterson. Taught him the violin and drum. And then he married his daughter.
And then George Peterson's son is Harold?
Right. His son is Harold and then there's little Harold who has the music of Moods band.
It's hard for me to keep all that family straight. Well... Oh, can be gentle.

There were about eight or nine children, you see. And Raymond Burke's mother was one of the Cassard girls. Harold Peterson's mother was one of the Cassards and my mother was a Cassard. There were only those girls. And there was a Joe Cassard. That's right. And that's her brother, Joe Cassard. Captain Cassard. And he was captain of the police. The police. And Jules and, let's see, Lucian and Leo, Leo Cassard.
He didn't know Cass, Joe the Cass, the banjo player. The mother boy, yeah.
I never met him.
I've heard of him. Joe had Raymond mentioned him.

I think I've seen his picture with him. Sure, he was Raymond. He told me, but he had a stroke and he's in a coma. He's been in a coma for about two or three years. But he was a terrific banjo player, guitar player.
Let's see, Leo played banjo. Jules played bass and trombone and maybe piano.

Jules played most everything. Anything. He played piano too. He told us he rolled on the floor with the bass one night because he didn't know how to play it and he just hammed it up. And then Joe played guitar and sang. Bertie played piano. And Roni played piano. That's Raymond's mother. My mother didn't play in musical instruments. And the grandfather was the one who played in the French opera. He played French horn and violin and hornet, I believe. They used to have a party just when they'd get together.
Oh, yeah. But Raymond was a barrier also, isn't it?
Well, Raymond's mother was married before and then she married Mr. Burke and he adopted Raymond.
I see. And so, then, I don't know, were any of Raymond's brothers musical or anything? No.
Nobody in the family. Raymond was more musical than the rest of them. They sing but they're not aggressive.
